utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-08-91-T. The Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. May we have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Joanna Korner assisted by Crispian Smith Case Manager for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Slobodan Cvijetic, and Eugene O'Sullivan appearing for Stanisic Defence this afternoon. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. For Zupljanin Defence this afternoon, Igor Pantelic, Dragan Krgovic, Jason Antley, and Miroslav Cuskic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we resume there are three brief matters which the Chamber wishes to address. On the 9 of April, 2010, the Prosecution filed a supplemental motion seeking to add one document to the exhibit list in relation to ST-125. Given that this witness will begin testifying today, could the Defence indicate now what its position is, or if they are unable to do so, we would request a response by the end of the earliest break today. Second matter: The Trial Chamber is seised of the Prosecution motion of the 1st of April, seeking additional time for the examination in chief of twelve Rule 92 ter witness. The motion is oversized; the Prosecution seeks an extension of the word limit to 4.618 words. The practice direction and the length of leaves and motions requires parties to seek leave in advance, stating the exceptional circumstances that necessitate the oversized filing. It is every party's duty to plan its motion practice according to applicable rules and procedures including this practice direction. The Chamber is not persuaded the Prosecution has established the existence of exceptional circumstances that would warrant granting the extension. The motion is therefore dismissed without prejudice to the Prosecution filing a new motion in accordance with the practice direction. Finally, on the 9th of April, the Prosecution filed a motion requesting that ST-176 be heard via video conference link. The Chamber orders the Defence to provide an oral response on the 15th of April. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just say something about this. So far numbers and, indeed, virtually every motion we filed so far recently has been rejected. And one of the major grounds for rejection has been we haven't supplied enough information. So we, in an effort to explain chapter and verse of why we are making the application for further time, we gave as much information as it was humanly possible. Now, it does seem to be, Your Honours, we can't win. If we stick to the word limit, then we can't give the information. We were told to file in advance the reasons why we were asking for more than 20 minutes. Are Your Honours saying it was simply that it was exceeded too much and that you are prepared to entertain a lesser, if there's such a word, exceeding of the word limit? Because I just don't know what we can do. Either we give the information that you want, or we are bound by the word limit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Korner, of course, we can't anticipate what ruling we would give on your re-filed motion. What we are saying is that there is a practice direction. The -- what we have doesn't adequately justify the exceeding the word limit, and we are inviting you to refile.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I understand that. Do I understand that Your Honours want a separate motion first, asking that we can exceed the word limit and explaining the reasons for that, and then when you grant it, then file the actual motion? Is that what you are suggesting?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: That appears to be the sequence that the practice direction anticipates.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Because equally, I mean, the same really applies to leave to respond to a reply to a motion that, technically, under the rules, we should first of all apply for leave to respond to the motion and then give the response. But, in fact, the practice has grown up that the two are combined as one, and it's simply of ease of reference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, the practice that you have referred to is perfectly legitimate and is well made in the interests of expediency. What we are requiring in this case is that we think that you could have easily submitted your motion and all the arguments in support of the extension of time for these 65 -- 92 ter witnesses, within the word limit, and we ask you to do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honours, I've heard the ruling, and we will we'll certainly do that. All I can say is that I hope that the response won't come that we haven't given enough information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So could we revert to closed session and have the witness escorted back to the stand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 15th day of April, 2010, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.59 p.m.
